title: Nine Inches and a Leg
subtitle: 椅子与座位 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 椅子与座位（生活与学习·家居与器物）
meta: 主题语境：椅子与座位（生活与学习·家居与器物）　|　核心词汇：chair　|　正文 337 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 chair 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1946 my mother was sent to mend ① chair she could not sit in, and she said the mending was the whole of the lesson. The ② chair, meaning the seat and not the room, was nine inches low and was mended by whoever came last; chair, she said, is the only thing in a house that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ chair in that house had the same leg, and the ④ chair at the end, meaning the one the carpenter kept and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever mended properly. Chair, my grandmother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the patience is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ chair was the whole of the meeting, meaning the seat of authority and not the furniture. The ⑥ chair, meaning the seat of authority and not any of that, is the only thing in a meeting that everybody defers to and nobody questions; chair, he said, is either something you mend or the only word that means both a seat and authority. She said the authority is the part they remember.

By 1961 the ⑦ chair had become a number in a report, and the report had become an argument about the leg. The ⑧ chair of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nine inches and eleven years of mending; chair, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ chair I remember is the one at the end, which was mended in 1966 and is still described as the straightest in the county. A ⑩ chair, my grandmother said in 1971, is the only thing that improves by being mended; every chair, she said, is authority that has agreed to look like a seat. She said the authority was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 椅子（指那个座位本身，与整个房间相对）
C. 固定搭配：mend a chair 修理一把椅子
D. n. 椅子（指房子里每一把）
E. n. 椅子（指末尾那一把）
F. n. 主席席位（抽象：它代表的那个权威）
G. n. 那个权威（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: chair she could not sit in
The chair, meaning the seat and not the room
chair was the whole of the meeting
The chair, meaning the seat of authority
the chair had become a number in a report
The chair of the whole thing

answers.why: mend a chair 意为“修理一把椅子”，1946 年母亲被派去修理她坐不进去的那把椅子。
chair 意为“椅子”，指那个座位本身而不是整个房间，矮了九英寸，由最后来的人修理。
chair 指房子里每一把椅子，每一把都是同样的腿。
chair 指末尾那一把（木匠保留的那一把），是唯一有人认真修理过的。
chair 意为“主席席位”，抽象指它代表的那个权威，父亲说 chair 就是那场会议的全部。
chair 为抽象用法，指那个权威本身，是一场会议里人人都听、却没人质疑的东西。
chair 意为“椅子”，到 1961 年这把 chair 成了报告里的一个数字。
chair 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九英寸和十一年的修理。
chair 意为“椅子”，我记得的是末尾那一把，1966 年修理过，至今仍被说成全县最端正的。
chair 为抽象总称，祖母说一把椅子是唯一会因为被认真修理而变好的东西。
